h: Teshuvah Opens the Heart to Torah and Lasting Holiness

p: On the Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah,
when it is already "let the year and its blessings begin"
(as was explained in the previous parshah),
the parshah of teshuvah is read,
for Shabbos is a time of teshuvah.
And on this Shabbos is the time
to rectify all that passed in the past year,
and through this we will merit
that "the year and its blessings begin."
"And it will be, when there come," etc.,
"and you take it to your heart
where Hashem your God has driven you."
is being led astray from the way of Hashem,
"and they led astray the inhabitants of their city."
And it says that the beginning of the awakening of teshuvah
is "and you take it to your heart
where Hashem your God has driven you":
to know that the leading astray came about
וּכְעֵין שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת לב, א)
"Were it not for these three verses," etc.;
For such was the beginning of Creation:
וּכְעֵין שֶׁאָמַר בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קפד, א)
and similar to what it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 184a):
except that which comes out of darkness."
"And you will return to Hashem your God."
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים מִזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
as has been explained several times from the holy Zohar;
that the Name Havayah is your leader.
until you know that the Name Havayah
"And you will listen to His voice":
this follows what we said (in the previous parshah),
that this is why it is mentioned everywhere:
"And it will be, if you will surely listen
to the voice of Hashem your God,"
only at the time of Matan Torah;
to what they said (Avos chapter 6, Avos 6:2):
"Every day a heavenly voice goes forth
for the insult to the Torah."
And this remained from the voices of Matan Torah,
שֶׁעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר שָׁם (שְׁמוֹת כ, טו)
of which it is said there (Shemos 20:15):
"And all the people see the voices":
in the heart of every one of Yisrael,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב מֵהַבַּעַל שֵׁם טוֹב זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
as is written in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory.
And in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 126a):
שׁוּבוּ בָּנִים שׁוֹבָבִים וְגוֹמֵר (יִרְמְיָה ג, יד)
and there is no one who inclines his ear."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה טו, א)
And this is along the lines of what they said (Chagigah 15a):
"I have already heard from behind the curtain:
and this is the heavenly voice
And then it was "except for Acher";
and it is stated (in the holy Shelah and in Sefer Reishis Chochmah)
that Acher was only not helped
and there is no one who pays attention."
וְהוּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבְּרֹאשׁ הַפָּרָשָׁה מַתְחִיל (מִשְׁלֵי א, כ–כב)
And this is because the beginning of that passage opens (Mishlei 1:20–22):
"Wisdom cries aloud in the street," etc.,
And this is "and you will listen to His voice
according to all that I command you today":
for every day the heavenly voice goes forth
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בְּפָרָשָׁה הָעֲבָרָה כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים
as it wrote several times in the previous parshah:
הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ מְצַוְּךָ וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים כו, טז)
"This day Hashem your God commands you," etc. (Devarim 26:16);
אֶת ה׳ הֶאֱמַרְתָּ הַיּוֹם וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם, יז)
"And Hashem has distinguished you today," etc. (Devarim 26:18);
הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה נִהְיֵיתָ לְעָם וְגוֹמֵר (שָׁם כז, ט)
"This day you have become a people," etc. (Devarim 27:9).

p: וְאָמַר כְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר אָנֹכִי מְצַוְּךָ הַיּוֹם
And it says, "according to all that I command you today":
בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ) (דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ח, ו)
in Midrash Rabbah (on this parshah) (Devarim Rabbah 8:6):
It was given together with all its tools of craft:
its uprightness, and the giving of its reward."
And the meaning of "its tools of craft"
is what the words of Torah
And for this it enumerated four things;
and it is along the lines of what we request:
"May He open our heart to His Torah,
and place in our heart love of Him and fear of Him,
and serve Him with a whole heart."
"May He open our heart to His Torah":
that is, that the words of Torah enter the heart;
for if a person is haughty,
לֹא יוּכְלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לִכְנוֹס בַּלֵּב
words of Torah cannot enter the heart,
"Just as water leaves a high place
and goes to a low place,
so too words of Torah endure
only in one whose mind is lowly."
And the haughtiness in a person's heart
שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנְסוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְתוֹךְ לִבּוֹ
so that words of Torah cannot enter his heart;
"May He open our heart to His Torah."
"And place in our heart love of Him and fear of Him"
corresponds to "the giving of its reward";
for this is the reward of the Torah,
that Hashem Yisbarach illuminates a person's heart
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach;
and this is "and place in our heart love of Him and fear of Him."
which brings one to be righteous
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיְּקַיֵּים כָּל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
by fulfilling all the words of Torah;
for if, chas v'shalom, one transgresses
as is written in the Gemara (Yevamos 20a).
And afterward, "and serve Him with a whole heart,"
"and for the upright of heart, gladness";
that is, to straighten the heart entirely,
along the lines of what they said (Berachos 59a):
to straighten the crookedness of the heart,
'And God has made it so that they fear Him.'"
"The precepts of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart."
And in the Gemara (end of the first chapter of Taanis, Taanis 15a):
"and for the upright of heart, gladness."
That is, through the precepts of Hashem
"and serve Him with a whole heart":
שֶׁיְּהֵא אַף הַלֵּב כְּסִיל גַּם כֵּן טוֹב
so that even the fool's heart will also be good,
and to empty the bad out of it entirely,
and the service will be with both hearts;
וּבַמִּדְרָשׁ חָשַׁב מַתַּן שְׂכָרָהּ (דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ח, ו)
And in the Midrash it counted "the giving of its reward" (Devarim Rabbah 8:6)
for a person does not merit the giving of its reward,
which is "and place in our heart love of Him and fear of Him,"
that come from the side of man;
namely, that he be lowly in his own estimation,
and straighten the crookedness of the heart,
when I bestow greatness upon you,
And this does not speak of greatness in this world,
like the greatness of Nevuchadnetzar and Sancheriv there,
for this was not reckoned as greatness at all
in matters of attainments and lofty levels,
his two kidneys like two teachers,
and they would well forth and teach him
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לְכָל הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
and through this he merited all the words of Torah.
And this is "may He open our heart to His Torah,"
שֶׁהוּא הַתְחָלַת כְּלֵי אוּמָּנוּתָהּ שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה
which is the beginning of the Torah's tools of craft,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ זוֹכִין לְג׳ הַדְּבָרִים הָאֲמוּרִים
and afterward one merits the three things mentioned.
And this is what is said:
"And you will listen to His voice
according to all that I command you";
that is, just as at the time
that Moshe Rabbeinu spoke this parshah,
he brought about that it entered their hearts;
he said that they would merit always to listen,
that it would always enter their hearts,
"according to all that I command you today";
וְהַיְינוּ וְכָל כְּלֵי אוּמָּנוּתָהּ שֶׁל הַתּוֹרָה
and that is "with all the tools of craft" of the Torah.

p: even though the statement is addressed to the last generation,
"And it will be, when there come upon you
and if so, with the word "you"
it already speaks to the children too.
that the teshuvah and the listening to His voice
that the bad will be uprooted completely,
until the children who will be born
will be so at the root, from birth.
Just as a person begets a person,
and each one in his own likeness,
so will the children be born
And this is "you and your children,"
that they will be born in holiness.
אִיתָא בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רסז, א)
it is stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 267a):
"'With all' — what does it speak of?
It should have said 'with your heart,'" etc.;
with the good inclination and with the evil inclination."
דְּדָרַשׁ אִישׁ נָבוּב יִלָּבֵב (אִיּוֹב יא, יב)
which expounds "a hollow man will gain heart" (Iyov 11:12):
before he has eaten and drunk
it appears that from "your heart" alone
it is expounded as "with both your inclinations,"
And if so, according to the Gemara's exposition,
is along the lines of what the Rishonim said,
And there is proof for this
וַיְהִי רָעָב בְּכׇל הָאֲרָצוֹת (בְּרֵאשִׁית מא, נד)
"'And there was famine in all the lands' (Bereishis 41:54):
הֲרֵי דְּדָרַשׁ מִתֵּיבַת בְּכׇל עַל ג׳
Thus it expounds the word "in all" as three.
that is, in each of the two hearts
namely, to empty out the bad
from "the heart of the fool, at his left" (Koheles 10:2),
which are the opposite of life,
into "the heart of the wise man, at his right":
the holiness of the three Avos,
who stand opposite the three kelipos mentioned,
as has been explained several times;
and this is "with all your heart."
"And Hashem your God will return," etc.;
"Return to Me, and I will return to you."
"And He will have mercy on you":
to gather our dispersed from among the nations;
and this is "and He will again gather you," etc.,
"where Hashem your God has scattered you."
Here it does not say "where He has driven you,"
אָז לֹא יִהְיֶה עוֹד נִדָּחִים מִדֶּרֶךְ ה׳
they will no longer be led astray from the way of Hashem;
only they are still scattered among the nations,
and Hashem Yisbarach will gather us.
And the parshah of teshuvah is read
on the Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah,
for Shabbos is a time of teshuvah,
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem";
"But one who confesses and forsakes will find mercy."
And on Shabbos one can merit
which are the Torah's tools of craft.
שֶׁכֵּן נִדְרָשׁ בְּתַנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ (רֵישׁ סֵדֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה)
for so it is expounded in Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu (at the beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah)
as referring to the day of Shabbos.
And on Shabbos every one of Yisrael becomes
"The awe of Shabbos is upon the unlearned person";
and he becomes poor and broken-spirited,
מַה שֶּׁעָשָׂה נֶגֶד רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
what he did against the will of Hashem Yisbarach
all the days of the week;
and he merits "its humility" and righteousness,
as it says in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 48):
Fortunate is one who makes for them
in the two chambers of the heart,
and the evil inclination is cleared out from there."
And this is "for the upright of heart, gladness,"
that Hashem Yisbarach dwells in the heart,
and this is the Upper Shabbos.
And one who merits the Upper Shabbos
as has been explained several times,
that this is the matter of two Shabbosos,
and one who merits them on a single Shabbos
on the Shabbos before Rosh Hashanah,
so that through this we will merit
that there be "my light" on Rosh Hashanah,
which is "enlighten our eyes in Your Torah,"
and "place in our heart love of Him and fear of Him,"
which is "the giving of its reward,"
